questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: my choice in picking Córdoba was because I have family in Torremolinos(close to Málaga) and I wanted to be closer to them. I also had a wish about learning more about my Andalusian heritage and the culture where I have family and roots.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The entire proces has been confusing, poorly constructed and I have felt like I stood alone with all my questions, problems and troubles with the application, both universities(KU and UCO). I have enjoyed being close to my family, but it has been insanely hard to feel this lonely and left alone with university informations.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was hard and difficult. KU did a slightly better job, but the proces feels unnecessary difficult and all the different steps, webpages and applications are a chaos of confusing. It feels like it can be made more efficient and I cannot be the first or last to feel this way.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive assistens when I arrived. I got a email regarding registration, that I did upon arrival. I did not receive and introduction to the system, the norms or the academic life on the university. I felt thrown into it without being able to find out what or where. Everthing I got to know about the system I found out myself or by asking other erasmus students. The only "introduction-invitation" I got was to an event that was at the same time as my classes, I there had to choose to get an introduction to my class(and exams) or an introduction that I didn't know was going to be academic related or personal-get-to-know-each-other-as -Erasmus-students related. It felt stupid to plan those two things at the same time and I went to the introduction to the class and exams. In hindsight I cannot tell which one had been best.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It seemed as the mobility office was too busy and there was ALWAYS a line and a long waiting time to get to the office. It felt like they assumed that we knew everything on forehand and that they didn't took into consideration that we where from different backgrounds, contries, norms, study life and approach to how to study at the university.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy and it was obvious that the city was used to have erasmus students. I used the company "Interasmundo" and it worked amazing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should know that you most likely will live with non-spanish-speaking students, so the main language is english.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: With interasmundo everything was easy, proper and non confusing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was always a long line, they took forever to answer emails and it was difficult to find informations.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: there was a poster next to the office with 5-6 steps, but many of the steps contained pages, systems that we hadn't got an introduction to. One of the steps was to send a email with some papers as: arrival, contract, insurance etc. but we never got an confirmation on the email, so we didn't know if was okay or not. We just had to keep cool and hope everything was okay, but without knowing for sure.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email and an office that had open from 9 -13 from monday to friday. But always with a line and waiting time.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I didn't have to apply for other classes because it all fitted into my schedule.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's important to look at what kind of exam there is to the class. And also to look at the requirements for the class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had courses that were all in relation to each other regarding art, movies, literature or linguistics. It was a good combination because they supported each other in material and content.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was confusing, different and felt like taking high school all over again. There was almost no text or material to support the classes. It was most of all ONLY the word of the professor or resumes of original text that we had as citation on powerpoints. It felt anti-academic and very high school like. I did not have a single book and in many classes I just had to write down what the professor was saying in contrast to actually support it with academic writings and books.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Cine Español, Literatura Comparada, Filosofia del Lenguaje, Variación Lingüística, Cine y su relación con las artes.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Cine Español. The professor was amazing and it included the spanish history, culture and creative life.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: only a broken phone, but otherwise nothing.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The train in between Córdoba and Málaga with Renfe. The cost was between 20-40 euros with train.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I swim on a competition level, and wanted therefor to swim at the swimteam at the university. I didn't happen because I was never able to register at the sport-page and when I called, they said the team was full.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was advertisement for sport and clubs, but I never figured out how and the informations for Erasmus students was very poorly done - there was never anything that told us about the social activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The city is amazing, and during the spring there is a lot of festivals. I would recommend the wine festival, la feria, las cruces de mayo. But these were not in relation the my host university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: the hikes close to Córdoba or to see Sevilla, Málaga, Granada and other places in Andalusia. Córdoba is a great city and the people living there is so amazing and welcoming.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Outside of the university it was easy because people was so sweet and I got some friends that were also on Erasmus.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The local students didn't really wanted to spend a lot of time with us. It felt like they were very used to Erasmus students and perhaps also used to many Erasmus students only wanting to party. This was not my case, I wanted to know more, and to learn more.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That students and professors are often late and that it's more chill.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness, the food, the way that the people are sweet and welcoming outside of university, the way of looking at life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The language will become better, the city is amazing and the Andalusian culture is so heartwarming and fun.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would tell them to try not to stress over the confusing and the difficulties, it will keep being confusing so no need to stress.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being close to my family and having the possibly to speak to them more often.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The entire proces.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
